reviewBoundary: Three grade7 fifteen-sentence form sets, three grade8 twelve-choice sets and three grade9 ten-choice sets:111 scoring items in9 complete practices. Station/farm/cafe, chess/picnic/scenery, leaflet/concert/town contexts. Same-author complete-option and accepted-variant review; counts are scoring slots, not distinct grammar concepts; no independent calibration.

units.title: Fifteen sentences: at the railway station
units.instruction: Complete all fifteen independent sentences. Ungiven gaps take ONE word; supplied-word gaps take the correct form, without an extra one-word limit.
units.alignmentNote: Complete fifteen-sentence form set. Five unprompted positions1/4/9/12/15 and ten supplied-word positions retained; no claim of distinct concepts for every scoring item.

materials.title: Fifteen sentences: at the railway station
materials.text: The fifteen sentences are independent. Use each sentence’s full context; a supplied word appears in brackets.

questions.prompt: Choose one way home: by train ____ by bus.
The children have tickets. ____ (they) tickets are in a small envelope.
There ____ (be) one information desk beside the entrance now.
The train leaves ____ ten thirty this morning.
There are two ____ (woman) at the information desk.
The suitcase belongs to Felix. It is ____ (Felix) suitcase.
questions.explanation: The owner name needs a possessive ending.

questions.prompt: We passed three ____ (bus) outside the station.
questions.explanation: Three requires the accepted plural buses/busses.

questions.prompt: Please ____ (keep) your ticket until the journey ends.
—____ platform do we need, platform one or platform two? —Platform two.
questions.explanation: Which selects between the two named platforms.

questions.prompt: The visitor is reading a ____ (Japan) newspaper.
questions.explanation: Japanese modifies newspaper; Japan is a country noun.

questions.prompt: Please speak ____ (quiet) in the waiting room.
questions.explanation: Quietly or informal flat quiet modifies speak.

questions.prompt: There is ____ information board above the doorway.
questions.explanation: Information begins with a vowel sound.

questions.prompt: The assistant showed ____ (we) the way to the platform.
We hope ____ (arrive) before lunchtime.
We stayed together ____ the station was crowded.
questions.explanation: Reason conjunctions introduce the finite clause.

materials.title: Fifteen sentences: a farm visit
materials.text: The fifteen sentences are independent. Use each sentence’s full context; a supplied word appears in brackets.

questions.prompt: Choose one activity: draw the sheep ____ sketch the barn.
The farmer has a dog. ____ (he) dog is beside the gate.
There ____ (be) exactly four ducks beside the pond now.
The small barn is ____ the two tall trees, with one tree on each side.
questions.explanation: Between matches the specified two-sided position.

questions.prompt: Two ____ (sheep) are standing under the tree.
questions.explanation: Sheep has the same singular and plural form.

questions.prompt: The green coat belongs to Sara. It is ____ (Sara) coat.
questions.explanation: The owner name needs possessive form.

questions.prompt: There are six ____ (tomato) in the basket.
Do not ____ (feed) the animals unless the guide permits it.
—____ is the little dog? —Behind the gate.
Our guide tells us about ____ (Australia) farms.
The farmer closed the gate ____ (careful).
We saw ____ unusual chicken with very curly feathers.
questions.explanation: Unusual starts with a vowel sound.

questions.prompt: The guide gave ____ (they) a map of the farm.
I would like ____ (visit) the vegetable garden next.
questions.explanation: Would like takes a to-infinitive, including a possible progressive.

questions.prompt: We waited by the barn ____ the guide returned.
questions.explanation: Until/till marks the endpoint; before also describes prior waiting. During cannot introduce the clause.

questions.prompt: The café serves ____ (Mexico) food on Fridays.

materials.title: Twelve choices: the chess club
materials.text: Read each sentence or short conversation in full. Choose one complete option per item.

questions.prompt: Lena has a chess set. ____ set is in the cupboard.
questions.explanation: Her determines set; the other pronoun forms do not.

questions.prompt: The club meets ____ Friday evenings.
questions.explanation: A named day with evening takes on.

questions.prompt: The library room was busy, ____ we moved to the hall.
This board is much ____ than the travel board.
questions.explanation: Much plus than requires comparative larger.

questions.prompt:
—Must I bring my own set?
—No, you ____. The club has enough.
questions.explanation: Needn’t removes obligation; the alternatives have different meanings.

questions.prompt:
—____ did the match end?
—At five o’clock.
Our coach usually ____ the rules before beginners play.
questions.explanation: A habitual present singular subject takes explains.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, we ____ a new strategy with the teacher.
At four yesterday, I ____ a game when the teacher arrived.
questions.explanation: The ongoing past action takes was watching.

questions.prompt: If the hall is free tomorrow, we ____ the final there.
questions.explanation: Future real condition takes will play.

questions.prompt: Of all six players, Mia thought ____.
questions.explanation: Six-person ranking calls for a superlative adverb.

questions.prompt: The coach asked us ____ the pieces after the game.
questions.explanation: Ask someone to collect takes infinitive.

questions.prompt: Please give the bottle to Omar. It belongs to ____.
questions.explanation: Belong to takes object him for the owner.

questions.prompt: The picnic took place ____ June.

questions.explanation: Because introduces the reason for moving.

questions.prompt: The empty bag is ____ than it was before lunch.

—____ I carry every box myself?
—No, you needn’t. We will share them.

—____ shall we put the empty bottles?
—In this labelled bag.
Our class always ____ the picnic place before leaving.
questions.explanation: The habitual singular collective class takes checks here.

questions.prompt: Last Saturday, we ____ the boxes back to school.
At two yesterday, we ____ the bags when the bus arrived.
questions.explanation: Past ongoing packing is interrupted by arrival.

questions.prompt: If the weather is dry next week, we ____ another outdoor lesson.
questions.explanation: Future real condition takes will have.

questions.prompt: Of the four groups, ours worked ____.
We hope ____ the same place next month.

questions.prompt: We have a large sheet. ____ sheet is on the floor mat.

—Must we paint the whole background today?
—No, you ____. We have another session.

—____ did you choose blue?
—Because the scene shows the sea.
questions.explanation: Because supplies the reason asked by Why.

questions.prompt: Our teacher usually ____ a sample before we begin.
questions.explanation: A present routine with singular teacher takes shows.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ____ the outlines before lunch.
At three yesterday, we ____ the sea when the bell rang.
questions.explanation: Ongoing past painting takes were painting.

questions.prompt: If the paint is dry tomorrow, we ____ the scenery to the hall with staff help.
questions.explanation: The future real result takes will move.

questions.prompt: Of all five groups, ours cleaned the brushes ____.
questions.explanation: Five groups call for superlative adverb.

questions.prompt: The teacher reminded us ____ our names on the work record.
questions.explanation: Remind someone to write takes infinitive.

materials.title: Ten choices: a museum leaflet
materials.text: Read each sentence or short conversation in full. Choose one complete option per item.

questions.prompt: The leaflet describes ____ unusual object from ____ European collection.
questions.explanation: Unusual takes an; European begins with /j/ and takes a.

questions.prompt: If the leaflet ____ today, visitors will receive it tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The leaflet receives printing, present passive in a real condition.

questions.prompt: The leaflet gives clear ____ to the nearest accessible entrance.
questions.explanation: Directions give a route to an entrance.

questions.prompt: Please label the map ____ so visitors can read it.
This room ____ contain the exhibition, but we should check the current notice.
questions.explanation: May fits tentative location needing confirmation.

questions.prompt: The staff printed exactly ____ leaflets:299 plus one.
questions.explanation: Exact300 is three hundred without plural/of.

questions.prompt: ____ the leaflet is short, it includes the main access information.
questions.explanation: Although marks concession between brevity and useful coverage.

questions.prompt: Don’t ____ the old map. If you ____ it, visitors may use the closed entrance.
questions.explanation: Imperative and real-condition present use display.

questions.prompt: The staff member ____ checked the route approved the map.

—Could you tell me ____?
—At the north entrance.
options: where do visitors collect the leaflet
whether do visitors collect the leaflet
what time visitors collect the leaflet
questions.explanation: A place answer needs embedded where with statement order.

questions.prompt: The teacher offered useful ____ for improving our rehearsal plan.

That case ____ belong to the violinist, but let’s ask before moving it.
There are exactly ____ seats, not199.
____ one player was absent, the group continued with a different piece.

questions.prompt: The musician ____ led the workshop also performed in the concert.

—Do you know ____?

—Could you tell me ____?
